metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code with entry points (ColdFusion .cfm files serving HTTP requests) and a database connection present. Single deployable unit running on IIS/EC2. Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: Database connections present (SQL Server via cfquery datasource); application manages document records with implied CRUD operations (search, download, upload implied by schema). Classified as stateful-crud.

top_gaps.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
top_gaps.gap: No IaC — all infrastructure is manually provisioned (ClickOps)
top_gaps.impact: Cannot reproduce environments, no disaster recovery, no audit trail for infrastructure changes

top_gaps.title: CI/CD Automation
top_gaps.gap: No CI/CD pipeline — deployment is manual file copy over network share
top_gaps.impact: No quality gates, no automated testing, error-prone manual deployments

top_gaps.title: Secrets Management
top_gaps.gap: Hardcoded credentials (CF Admin password documented in README)
top_gaps.impact: Critical security vulnerability — credentials exposed in version control

top_gaps.title: Monolith vs Microservices
top_gaps.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith with SQL embedded in presentation layer
top_gaps.impact: Cannot independently scale, deploy, or maintain components

top_gaps.title: Encryption at Rest
top_gaps.gap: No encryption at rest — documents on local disk without encryption
top_gaps.impact: Data exposure risk for policy documents and internal forms

findings.title: No managed compute — all workloads on raw EC2
findings.description: All compute runs on a single raw EC2 instance (Windows Server 2008) with IIS 7 and Adobe ColdFusion 8. No managed container orchestration or serverless is used.
findings.gap: No managed compute services in use. 100% of workload on unmanaged EC2 with an EOL operating system.
findings.recommendation: Replatform the application to a modern runtime and deploy on ECS/Fargate or Lambda.

findings.title: Self-managed database on EOL engine
findings.description: Database is SQL Server 2005 self-managed on EC2. No managed database services (RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB) in use.
findings.gap: Self-managed database on an EOL engine with no automated failover, backups, or patching.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS for SQL Server or Aurora PostgreSQL via AWS DMS.

findings.title: No workflow orchestration
findings.description: No workflow orchestration service in use. All logic is inline in CFM files with no multi-step orchestration.
findings.gap: No orchestration tooling. Future multi-step workflows would be entirely hardcoded.
findings.recommendation: When replatforming, use AWS Step Functions for any multi-step document workflows.

findings.title: No async messaging infrastructure
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. All operations are synchronous HTTP. No SQS, SNS, EventBridge, or message broker in use.
findings.gap: No async messaging for state changes that would benefit from decoupling.
findings.recommendation: Implement SNS/SQS for document lifecycle events when replatforming.

findings.title: No network security controls
findings.description: No evidence of VPC, private subnets, or security groups. Application runs HTTP only with no encryption in transit and no network segmentation.
findings.gap: No network isolation, no HTTPS, no security groups. Services deployed without proper network controls.
findings.recommendation: Deploy in a VPC with private subnets, least-privilege security groups, and HTTPS via ALB.

findings.title: No managed API entry point
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, CloudFront, or load balancer. Users access the application directly on EC2.
findings.gap: No managed entry point providing throttling, auth offload, or request validation.
findings.recommendation: Add API Gateway or ALB as entry point with WAF protection.

findings.title: No auto-scaling configured
findings.description: No auto-scaling. Single EC2 instance with static capacity. No ASG, no ECS auto-scaling.
findings.gap: Workload cannot respond to traffic changes. Single instance — reboot equals downtime.
findings.recommendation: Configure auto-scaling on compute layer when replatforming.

findings.title: No backup and recovery capability
findings.description: No backup configuration. README states 'no backups offsite' and 'disk loss = data loss.' Documents on local disk with no replication.
findings.gap: Complete absence of backup and recovery. Single disk failure causes permanent data loss.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to S3 with versioning and RDS with automated backups and PITR.

findings.title: No high availability or fault isolation
findings.description: All resources in a single instance with no multi-AZ deployment. Single point of failure for all components.
findings.gap: Single point of failure — any failure takes down the entire application with no automatic recovery.
findings.recommendation: Deploy across multiple AZs with ALB, RDS Multi-AZ, and S3 for document storage.

findings.title: Zero Infrastructure as Code coverage
findings.description: No IaC exists. Zero .tf files, CloudFormation templates, CDK stacks, or any IaC artifacts. All infrastructure manually provisioned.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. Cannot reproduce environment, no audit trail, no disaster recovery from definition.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in CloudFormation or CDK from the start of replatforming.

findings.title: No CI/CD automation — manual deployment
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Deployment is manual file copy over network share to wwwroot.
findings.gap: All deployments manual with no build, test, or approval stages. No rollback capability.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD with CodePipeline covering build, test, security scan, and deploy stages.

findings.title: EOL language with no cloud-native tooling
findings.description: Application written in CFML on Adobe ColdFusion 8 (EOL 2014). No AWS SDK, no cloud-native tooling, no container support.
findings.gap: ColdFusion 8 has no AWS SDK, no modern frameworks, and no path to cloud-native without full rewrite.
findings.recommendation: Replatform to Python 3.12+/FastAPI, Node.js 20+/Express, Java 21/Spring Boot, or .NET 8/ASP.NET Core.

findings.title: Tightly-coupled monolith with no boundaries
findings.description: Tightly-coupled monolith with SQL embedded in presentation layer. No module boundaries, no separation of concerns.
findings.gap: Pervasive shared state. Presentation, business logic, and data access mixed in same files.
findings.recommendation: Replatform with clean architecture — separate API, business logic, and data access layers.

findings.title: All communication synchronous with no async patterns
findings.description: All communication is synchronous HTTP. No async patterns, no message queues, no event-driven handlers.
findings.gap: No async communication for state changes that cross potential service boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Implement event-driven patterns for document lifecycle events using SNS/SQS or EventBridge.

findings.title: No long-running process handling
findings.description: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. No async job processing, no background workers.
findings.gap: No async job infrastructure for operations that may exceed 30 seconds.
findings.recommendation: Implement async processing for document uploads using SQS workers or Step Functions.

findings.title: No API versioning strategy
findings.description: No versioning. Application serves HTML pages directly with no version headers or URL versioning.
findings.gap: No versioning mechanism. Changes deployed directly with no backward compatibility guarantees.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-based versioning (/v1/documents) and OpenAPI specifications when replatforming.

findings.title: No service discovery — all endpoints hardcoded
findings.description: No service discovery. Database datasource hardcoded in CF Admin. File storage path hardcoded in source.
findings.gap: All service endpoints and resource locations hardcoded with no dynamic discovery.
findings.recommendation: Externalize configuration via environment variables or Parameter Store. Use Cloud Map for discovery.

findings.title: Documents stored on local disk — no object storage
findings.description: Documents stored on local disk (D:\docroot\files). No S3, no object storage, no parsing capabilities.
findings.gap: Data locked on local filesystem. No accessibility, no parsing pipeline, single point of failure.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon S3 with versioning. Implement Textract for document content extraction.

findings.title: No data access layer — inline SQL in presentation files
findings.description: Database queries scattered in presentation-layer .cfm files. No DAO, no repository pattern, no ORM.
findings.gap: SQL embedded in page files. No data contract enforcement, no query consistency.
findings.recommendation: Implement repository/DAO pattern with centralized data access layer when replatforming.

findings.title: Database engine critically past EOL
findings.description: SQL Server 2005 — EOL since April 2016. Over 10 years past end-of-life with known critical CVEs.
findings.gap: Engine critically past EOL. No security patches available. No version management strategy.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS SQL Server 2019/2022 or Aurora PostgreSQL.

findings.title: No encryption at rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest. Documents on local disk without encryption. Database has no TDE or KMS encryption.
findings.gap: Zero encryption at rest. Policy documents stored in plaintext on unencrypted disk.
findings.recommendation: Use S3 with SSE-KMS for documents and RDS/Aurora with KMS encryption enabled.

findings.title: Session-based auth without token-based security
findings.description: Application-managed session authentication. No OAuth2/JWT. Vulnerable to session fixation.
findings.gap: No token-based auth. Session-based with known session fixation vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT via Cognito with API Gateway authorizer.

findings.title: No centralized identity integration
findings.description: Application manages its own authentication entirely. No external IdP, no SSO, no federation.
findings.gap: No centralized identity integration. Separate credentials required.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito or existing enterprise IdP with SSO.

findings.title: Hardcoded credentials in version control
findings.description: ColdFusion Administrator password 'cfadmin' documented in README. No Secrets Manager, no Vault.
findings.gap: Credentials in version-controlled README. No secrets management, no rotation.
findings.recommendation: Remove credentials from VCS. Implement AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: No compute hardening — all software EOL
findings.description: No patching strategy. All software EOL: Windows Server 2008, ColdFusion 8, SQL Server 2005, IIS 7. Known critical CVEs unpatched.
findings.gap: All software past EOL with no patches available. No vulnerability scanning.
findings.recommendation: Replatform to supported software. Use managed services to eliminate patching burden.

findings.title: No application security pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools. No CI/CD to integrate them. Known SQL injection and XSS undetected by automation.
findings.gap: Zero security automation. No SAST, no DAST, no dependency scanning.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST and dependency scanning in CI/CD pipeline when built.

findings.title: No distributed tracing
findings.description: No tracing instrumented. No X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry, no trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: Zero tracing capability. Cannot trace requests or diagnose production issues.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with AWS X-Ray or OpenTelemetry when replatforming.

findings.title: No SLO definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no monitoring, no formal service level definitions.
findings.gap: Cannot measure whether system meets user expectations or is degrading.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for availability, latency, and error rate with CloudWatch monitoring.

findings.title: No business metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business metrics tracked for document portal usage.
findings.gap: Cannot measure portal usage, popular documents, or user engagement.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom CloudWatch metrics for documents_downloaded, search_queries, unique_users.

findings.title: No anomaly detection or alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection. Failures detected only by user reports.
findings.gap: No alerting. Failures and degradation go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms on error rates and latency with anomaly detection.

findings.title: No deployment strategy — direct-to-production file copy
findings.description: Direct-to-production deployment via manual file copy to wwwroot. No staged rollout, no health checks.
findings.gap: No deployment safety. Changes go live immediately with no validation or rollback.
findings.recommendation: Implement blue/green or canary deployments via AWS CodeDeploy.

findings.title: No automated tests of any kind
findings.description: No automated tests — no unit, integration, or end-to-end tests. No test framework configured.
findings.gap: Zero automated test coverage. No regression detection capability.
findings.recommendation: Implement integration tests for critical workflows from day one of replatforming.

findings.title: No incident response automation
findings.description: No runbooks, no automated remediation, no self-healing. Incident response entirely ad hoc.
findings.gap: No documented procedures for common failure scenarios.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks and implement automated recovery via ASG and SSM Automation.

findings.title: No observability ownership
findings.description: No dashboards, no alarms with owners, no CODEOWNERS file. No monitoring infrastructure exists to own.
findings.gap: No observability assets exist. No ownership model for service health.
findings.recommendation: Establish per-service dashboards with alarm ownership when replatforming.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — No stored procedures or proprietary SQL. All queries are standard SQL in application layer.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false. No IaC exists; CloudTrail is account-level and belongs in foundation repo.

evaluations.title: Resource Tagging Governance
evaluations.reason: has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false. No AWS resources provisioned from this repo — nothing to tag.

triggering_questions.note: DATA-Q4=4 meets threshold; no stored procedure migration blocker

pathways.not_triggered_reason: DATA-Q4=4 — no stored procedures or proprietary SQL detected. The simple standard SQL makes database engine migration straightforward without needing the Open Source pathway's stored procedure extraction guidance.

pathways.name: Move to Managed Databases

immediate_actions: Assess schema for Aurora PostgreSQL compatibility

pathways.name: Move to Managed Analytics

triggering_questions.note: INF-Q4=1 but contextual guard blocks: no streaming, ETL, or analytics artifacts found

pathways.not_triggered_reason: No data processing workloads found in the repository. The application is a simple document portal with no streaming, ETL, data pipeline, or analytics processing. The contextual guard requires evidence of data processing workloads.

decomposition_strategy.rationale: All-EOL stack (ColdFusion 8, SQL Server 2005, Windows Server 2008) makes Strangler Fig impractical. Application is small enough (2 source files, ~60 lines of logic) for a complete replatform as a well-structured modular application.
decomposition_strategy.effort_estimate: Medium — small application scope but requires new infrastructure setup
